name: security-circleci-context-authority-review
intent: CircleCI context secrets and workflow approval/source binding
artifacts: Config sources/orbs, context restrictions, project/branch identities and approval jobs.
trace: Determine whether a lower-trust config revision can execute a context-bearing job or change the artifact after an approval.
experiment: Use an isolated config/local execution fixture with synthetic context values and inert publication; compare authorized and untrusted source contexts.
disproof: A context name in config or an approval click is not proof the consumed revision was trusted.
repair: Bind contexts and approval to actual trusted job inputs, retesting legitimate release and fork/branch separation.
branch_decisions: Inspect context restrictions, project identity and approval job placement against the exact workflow revision. An approval event is not sufficient if a later untrusted script substitution changes what runs with the context. Fork/branch settings and expression restrictions may deny context access before execution; retain that denial as a specific negative control.
operational_method: Record which approving actor is permitted by a restricted context security group and which project/expression restrictions the context-bearing job must satisfy. Workflow approval and context access are distinct decisions. Compare an approved job whose actor/context eligibility fails with an eligible actor using the same source revision. Do not treat a green approval node as proof that secrets were injected or that the approver authorized a later substituted script.
